item.title: Hegseth favors Sean Parnell for Army secretary, sources say
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has told people close to him that Sean Parnell would be his top choice for secretary of the Army, several senior officials told CBS News.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy jury leaves without verdict, defense wants juror dismissed
item.description: A sixth day of jury deliberations in Lindsay Clancy's Massachusetts murder trial ended Thursday without a verdict.

item.title: Work on Trump-backed Triumphal Arch will start in coming weeks
item.description: The federal government plans to start excavation over the next two weeks on a massive triumphal arch near Washington, D.C., Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum said, a controversial project championed by President Trump.

item.title: Suspect in downtown Minneapolis mass shooting was facing eviction
item.description: The man suspected of killing two people and injuring six others in a mass shooting at a downtown Minneapolis apartment complex Wednesday was facing eviction after a string of incidents including assault and allegedly showing a gun to apartment management, according to court documents.

item.title: Vance says, "I wouldn't call it a war" when asked about Iran
item.description: Iran's latest attacks did not impact military facilities used by the U.S., military officials say, after Iran claimed it targeted U.S. forces in Kuwait. When Vice President JD Vance was asked about the conflict's timeline during a press briefing on Thursday, he stopped short of calling it a war. CBS News contributor Elliot Ackerman has more.

item.title: American automakers urge Congress to ban Chinese vehicle sales in U.S.
item.description: Chinese cars can collect and send consumer and vehicle data to Beijing, U.S. automaker group warns in calling for a ban on sales.

item.title: Officials lay out timeline of Minneapolis mass shooting
item.description: A gunman killed two people in downtown Minneapolis on Wednesday in a shooting that also injured five others. CBS News correspondent Jonah Kaplan reports.

item.title: Vance addresses high-profile military departures under Hegseth: "We needed to have a culture shift"
item.description: At the White House press briefing on Thursday, Vice President JD Vance discussed the high number of military departures under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's tenure. CBS News White House reporter Aaron Navarro has the details.

item.title: Vance "extremely skeptical" U.S. strike hit Iran wedding party
item.description: Iran responded to a warning from President Trump with claims of new strikes against U.S. forces in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates.

item.title: DOJ asks Supreme Court to allow Postal Service rules on mail ballots
item.description: The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to intervene in an ongoing legal battle over U.S. Postal Service rules for mail ballots just weeks before the November midterm elections.

item.title: The Social Security Administration overpaid her. Now she owes $35,000.
item.description: The agency told a woman that she has 30 days to pay it back. Otherwise, it would cut her benefits by 50% while it collects what it overpaid.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy jury ends tumultuous Day 6 of deliberations still deadlocked
item.description: The sixth day of jury deliberations in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial ended without a verdict after several tense moments in court. CBS News' Jessica Levinson and Shanelle Kaul have the latest.

item.title: Dozens of investment firm employees killed during 9/11 attack | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: The investment banking firm Sandler O'Neill faces the tragedy of 9/11. A third of its employees were killed in the attack on the World Trade Center.

item.title: Gas prices surge just before Labor Day, as diesel nears record high
item.description: "Diesel is just a couple of ticks away from hitting a new record," one energy expert said. "That will happen."

item.title: Missouri House candidate accused of conspiring to plant cocaine on opponent
item.description: Thomas Ross allegedly tried to get his campaign manager to plant cocaine and Adderall on his opponent, federal prosecutors in Missouri said.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's lawyer asks for juror to be removed as deliberations continue
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's defense on Thursday asked for a juror to be removed as deliberations continued for a sixth day. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul and Jessica Levinson have more.

item.title: CBS News gas and oil price tracker shows how much energy costs are rising
item.description: As the war with Iran continues, CBS News is tracking gas and oil prices. Find out how much more it costs to fill up your tank or heat your house.

item.title: Election officials raise alarm over mail voting rules: "Virtually impossible"
item.description: One official in California said that scanning individual ballots for every voter in the state would take roughly 43 years based on the Postal Service's estimates.

item.title: How much will a $150,000 HELOC cost monthly if opened now?
item.description: Want to borrow some of your equity via a HELOC? Here's what monthly payments on a $150,000 HELOC may look like now.

item.title: Postal Service mail voting rules face extended block as judge presses DOJ
item.description: A federal judge is considering whether to continue blocking a U.S. Postal Service rule imposing new requirements for mail voting.

item.title: CBS reporter tests London's first self-driving taxis
item.description: The first self-driving taxis have launched in London. Uber has 15 vehicles operating in the city with a required supervisor in the car. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry took an autonomous ride with Wayve co-founder and CEO Alex Kendall, whose AI technology is powering the robotaxis in London's iconic Westminster.

item.title: Watch: Vance holds White House press briefing, talks Iran and midterm elections
item.description: Vice President JD Vance on Thursday held the first White House press briefing since Karoline Leavitt departed as press secretary. Following the briefing, CBS News' Aaron Navarro provided further context.

item.title: Judge blocks Trump's latest effort to narrow birthright citizenship
item.description: A federal judge has temporarily blocked a Trump executive order that would prevent certain people from automatically becoming U.S. citizens at birth.

item.title: How much interest can a $100,000 6-month CD earn at today's rates?
item.description: A $100,000 6-month CD will provide short-term protection and a boost to your savings in 2027. Here's what to know.

item.title: Estrogen patch shortage prompts doctors, lawmakers to seek FDA action
item.description: Some patients and doctors are calling on the FDA to formally recognize a shortage of the medications, saying the agency's shortage database does not reflect problems they are seeing at pharmacies.

item.title: Trump $1 coins are now on sale. Here's how much they cost.
item.description: The U.S. Mint said the President Donald J. Trump $1 coin can be bought in packages of 25 for $61 or 100 coins for $154.50.

item.title: Clancy trial highlights need to rethink postpartum care: "The duty is on the system"
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's case is resonating with moms across the U.S. — bringing into focus the spectrum of perinatal mood and anxiety disorders​ and the lack of resources for many women.

item.title: When Social Security mistakenly overpays benefits, you might get a bill | 60 Minutes
item.description: Each year, about two million people are told they owe the Social Security Administration money because the agency miscalculated their benefits and paid them too much.

item.title: When Social Security mistakenly overpays benefits, you might get a bill | 60 Minutes
item.description: Each year, about a million people are told they owe the Social Security Administration money because the agency miscalculated their benefits and paid them too much.
